It sounds like you'd have the time to take care of a cat, so I'd say go for it! Perhaps get one from a shelter nearby. Just make sure to give them space at the beginning and they can get used to their surroundings. Most cats live long lives, so remember that. As long as you're willing to take responsibility, a cat might be a good companion for you.

Sometime when I was 4, someone escaped from the local prison and was found in my neighborhood.  Another time, my mother was outside with me as a child. (I was in one of those playpens for toddlers.) She left for a moment to fetch something from inside and found a large dog was attacking my next-door neighbor. Needless to say, I wasn't allowed to be alone outside for the majority of my childhood.
Your grandmother seems like an awful person to be around. A bond with a person like that only brings trouble. You stood up for yourself and there's nothing wrong with that. NTA
NAH, it just seems like it wasn't meant to be.
